articles.title: Brad Ausmus Hired as New Manager of Houston Astros
articles.summary: The Houston Astros have announced the hiring of Brad Ausmus as their new manager, marking a return to the team where he spent a significant portion of his playing career.
articles.content: The Houston Astros have announced the hiring of Brad Ausmus as their new manager, marking a return to the team where he spent a significant portion of his playing career. Ausmus played for 10 seasons with the Astros, making him one of the longest-tenured players in franchise history, and his 1,259 games behind the plate are still a record for catchers. His tenure is also notable for being the 10th most games played by any player in team history. Ausmus's playing career was marked by its longevity, with him spending time with four different franchises. During his time with the Astros, Ausmus developed a strong connection to the city and its fans, who will remember him fondly as one of their own. In fact, he has stated that Houston felt like his baseball home, even when he was drafted out of high school by the Yankees. It's clear that Ausmus's experience in Houston had a lasting impact on him. As Ausmus prepares to take on his new role as manager, fans and players alike will be looking back at his playing career for inspiration. His time with the Astros was marked by several notable moments, including a memorable home run he hit during the 2005 NLDS. The image of Ausmus rounding the bases after hitting that home run is one that will likely stick in the memories of Astros fans. Ausmus's playing career may be over, but his legacy as a player and now manager has only just begun to take shape. As he embarks on this new chapter, it remains to be seen what kind of impact he will have on the team and its fans. The Astros' 2005 National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves was a series that would be remembered for its thrilling conclusion. With the team trailing 6-1 in Game 4, Lance Berkman's grand slam in the eighth inning sparked a late-game surge, but the Astros still found themselves down by one run with two outs in the bottom of the ninth. It was then that Brad Ausmus came to the plate, delivering an unexpected blow. Despite having hit only three home runs during the regular season, Ausmus blasted a game-tying homer to left-center, tying the score and sending the game into extra innings. The Astros ultimately won the game and the series on Chris Burke's 18th-inning home run. This dramatic turn of events was just one of several memorable moments in Ausmus' time as an Astro player. Another notable instance came during the 2004 American League Championship Series against the St. Louis Cardinals, where a diving catch by Jim Edmonds robbed Ausmus of a hit in Game 7. The Astros nearly achieved their first World Series appearance in 2004, but it was not meant to be. In Game 7 against the St. Louis Cardinals, Brad Ausmus came close to delivering a crucial hit for his team. Houston took an early lead with two runs on the board in the second inning, and Ausmus's line drive to center field seemed destined to make it 3-0. However, Cardinals' center fielder Jim Edmonds made an impressive diving catch to halt the momentum. The Cardinals capitalized on this pivotal moment, mounting a comeback with three runs in the sixth inning that ultimately ended the Astros' season. The curtain call was a fitting tribute to Brad Ausmus' impressive performance at Minute Maid Park. Fans gave him a standing ovation not once, but twice - first after his home run and again when he left the game in the sixth inning. Ausmus himself reflected on the experience, describing it as one of the most memorable days of his life. But what stood out to him was not just the excitement of hitting a home run or making a crucial play, but rather the people and relationships that made those moments possible. As a player, Ausmus spent two years with the Dodgers before retiring from baseball. During his time with the Astros, he established himself as one of the team's top defenders, earning three Gold Glove awards in the process. His impressive defensive skills behind the plate have left a lasting legacy on the franchise. The impressive defensive skills behind the plate that have left a lasting legacy on the franchise are not the only notable aspect of Brad Ausmus' time with the Astros. Throughout his 17-year career with the team, he remarkably managed to avoid any significant injuries that would keep him out of action. It wasn't until his final season in the league that Ausmus faced a serious injury, undergoing surgery for a bulging disc in his back while playing for the Dodgers in 2010. The injury forced him to miss more than three months of play but he eventually returned to the field, albeit only for 18 games. The Astros had previously traded for Ausmus twice and dealt him away once as part of major package deals with the Detroit Tigers. In one notable trade, the team sent Ausmus back to the Tigers in exchange for a trio of players, including Paul Bako, Dean Crow, and Brian Powell. articles.title: Physical Activity Can Be Incorporated into Daily Routines with Simple Steps
articles.summary: Experts recommend incorporating physical activity into daily routines by starting with simple steps such as taking a walk or doing short periods of movement throughout the day.
articles.content: Experts recommend incorporating physical activity into daily routines, starting with something as simple as taking a walk. According to exercise physiologists, walking is an effective way to get moving and can be done anywhere, whether outside or on a treadmill or walking pad at home. Even short periods of walking can make a difference in overall health, such as taking a 10-minute stroll after dinner. By incorporating regular movement into daily activities, individuals can reduce the negative effects of prolonged sitting. Setting reminders to stand up and move is also crucial, with experts suggesting that setting alarms on watches or phones can be an effective way to stay active throughout the day. Planning social activities that promote physical activity is an effective way to reduce sedentary behavior. Instead of meeting friends for meals, consider organizing activities like yoga or dance classes, hiking trips, or playing sports together. Reframing our mindset around exercise is essential, as it's not necessary to commit a significant amount of time each session. Breaking up longer periods of activity into shorter intervals can be just as beneficial. For instance, doing a few sets of bicep curls, bodyweight squats, or jumping jacks during breaks can add up to a substantial workout. Even brief moments of movement can make a positive impact on our overall health and well-being. Taking short pauses throughout the day to stretch, move around, or do some light exercise can be as simple as taking two minutes out of your schedule. Taking short breaks to incorporate more movement into daily routines is recommended by experts as a way to improve overall health and happiness. One approach suggested is to aim for at least 10 minutes of physical activity, but even smaller intervals can be beneficial, particularly when it comes to general well-being. According to Chiodini, taking just two minutes to get up and move around can have a positive impact on one's mood and energy levels. When out running errands, experts advise making the most of opportunities for physical activity. For instance, instead of parking in a convenient spot near the entrance of a store, drivers are encouraged to park further away, such as at the back of the lot. This simple habit can lead to additional steps being taken throughout the day. Taking on household chores can be a great way to get some extra movement throughout the day. For example, doing yard work may seem like a mundane task, but it can actually burn a significant number of calories. In one instance, a person tracked their activity while weeding and was surprised to find they had burned nearly 500 calories after just two hours. Engaging in playful activities with children or pets is also an easy way to incorporate more movement into your daily routine. These activities not only provide entertainment but also opportunities for physical activity that are often enjoyable and effortless. Moreover, the benefits of yard work extend beyond calorie burn, as it also provides exposure to sunshine and fresh air. Taking the stairs instead of the elevator is another simple habit to adopt when possible. Experts suggest using just one step on a staircase to get some exercise, and even taking steps sideways or down can be beneficial. By incorporating these habits into daily life, individuals can make significant strides towards reducing their sedentary time and increasing overall physical activity. Individuals often struggle to maintain momentum when it comes to reducing sedentary time, and experts note that this is where most people tend to plateau. One way to increase physical activity without realizing it is through fidgeting, which can be a part of non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT). This subtle yet effective approach encourages individuals to move more throughout the day by incorporating small movements into their daily routine. As the body becomes accustomed to increased movement, individuals may find themselves wanting to add more activities to their daily schedule. articles.title: Veteran Actress Irma P. Hall Passes Away at Age 91
articles.summary: The family of Irma P. Hall announced her death on Wednesday, but did not provide a cause for her passing.
articles.content: Veteran actress Irma P. Hall has passed away at the age of 91. Her family announced the news on Wednesday, but did not provide a cause for her death. Hall's career spanned multiple decades and numerous iconic roles, including that of Big Mama in the 1997 film "Soul Food. In this role, she brought warmth and authority to the matriarchal character, earning an NAACP Image Award in the process. Her portrayal also led to a return as Big Mama in the television series based on the film. In addition to her work in Soul Food, Hall appeared in several other notable films, including The Ladykillers" and "A Family Thing. The latter marked a significant milestone for Hall, who was 60 years old when she landed a major film role as Aunt T., a blind woman offering guidance to two half brothers. Hall's performance in A Family Thing drew attention to her craft, which had been developing for years through work onstage and in smaller screen roles. Irma Hall's entry into acting was a gradual one, as she had initially set out for other pursuits. Born Irma Dolores Player on June 3, 1935, in Beaumont, Texas, she spent her formative years in Chicago before returning to Texas for college. Hall went on to become an educator, teaching English and foreign languages in Dallas public schools for over two decades. However, it was during this time that she began to explore her acting talents, with a notable early role coming when actor and director Raymond St. Jacques cast her in his 1973 film Book of Numbers after hearing her recite poetry in Dallas. As Hall's involvement in the arts grew, she continued to teach while taking on more acting roles. It wasn't until the 1980s that performance became her full-time focus. During this period, she also played a key role in establishing the Dallas Minority Repertory Theatre and remained committed to developing young artists. Hall's extensive career encompassed theater, television, and film, with notable credits including the 1997 Clint Eastwood drama Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil as well as the 1998 films Beloved" and "Patch Adams. Her voice work also included a role as Great Aunt T. in the 2001 Rugrats Kwanzaa special. Irma P. Hall was hospitalized after a 2004 car crash that left her with severe injuries, including open-heart surgery, a broken arm, and a crushed ankle. During her recovery at a Chicago convalescent center, she was invited to attend a private screening of The Ladykillers" and made the trip despite her fragile health. Hall expressed her admiration for the film, stating that it exceeded her expectations when seen on screen. A touching gesture from her friends in the entertainment industry came in the form of signed pillows from Tom Hanks and the Coen brothers, who had been keeping tabs on her well-being while she recuperated. Hall cherished these mementos as a reminder of their kindness and friendship. In addition to her acting career, Hall was also deeply committed to her faith community in Dallas, where she served as a Church Mother at Inspiring Body of Christ Church for many years. Her family remembered her as a devoted woman who used her talents to inspire children through reading and theater programs at the church's school. articles.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Large-Scale Prisoner Exchange
articles.summary: A breakthrough has been achieved in the ongoing peace talks between Russia and Ukraine as both sides agreed to a prisoner exchange.
articles.content: A major breakthrough has been achieved in the ongoing peace talks between Russia and Ukraine as both sides have agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange. The agreement was reached on Wednesday, marking the final day of two days of intense negotiations in Abu Dhabi that aimed to bring an end to the conflict in Ukraine. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will now play key roles in facilitating further talks between Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky. Witkoff and Kushner are set to meet separately with Putin and Zelensky on Thursday, a move that is seen as an effort to capitalize on any momentum gained from the Abu Dhabi talks. The US envoys will first travel to Moscow to meet with the Russian president before flying to Dublin, where they will brief Zelensky. Zelensky's visit to Ireland has also provided an opportunity for him to assess the prospects of a peaceful resolution to the conflict. Speaking on arrival in Dublin, he expressed cautious optimism that a "window of opportunity could be seized to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II before 2027. The Ukrainian leader welcomed what he described as a change in tone from the US regarding the inclusion of European nations in the Washington-mediated talks. He noted that the American side is now treating this aspect more positively, and expressed hope that this shift could lead to meaningful progress in the negotiations. The ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine has taken a complex turn as European countries grapple with Moscow's proposal to review the continent's security architecture. Russian negotiators have expressed their desire for a new, modern Yalta, a reference to the 1945 conference where Western leaders divided Europe with the Soviet Union. This ambitious goal suggests that Russia is seeking significant changes in its relationship with European countries. The upcoming meeting of 50 European leaders in Dublin will likely focus on the outcome of the Abu Dhabi talks and their implications for regional security. EU officials have expressed skepticism about any genuine progress towards peace, insisting that Europe should not engage in broader discussions with Moscow until fighting stops. NATO chief Mark Rutte has taken a more optimistic view, stating that the Abu Dhabi talks demonstrate unity among the US, Ukraine, and European countries. This alignment is seen as a positive development, but it remains to be seen whether it will translate into concrete progress in negotiations. European officials have emphasized that no decisions on naming a single envoy for potential talks with Moscow are expected at the Dublin meeting, leaving the choice of representation open-ended. The negotiations between Russia and Ukraine have delved deeper into the sensitive topic of security guarantees, with both sides providing more detailed explanations on their respective positions. Ukrainian negotiator David Arakhamia described the talks as challenging, noting that Russia's delegation arrived in Dublin with strict instructions. However, he emphasized that despite these difficulties, there is a growing momentum towards reaching a solution by year's end. The upcoming meeting between US officials and Russian President Putin will focus on building upon the discussions held in Abu Dhabi. Kushner has stated that the meeting aims to make further progress on key issues, which they believe hold promise for potential breakthroughs. In preparation for the next round of talks, Kyiv's main negotiator Umerov cautioned that significant work remains ahead, but expressed optimism about continuing the negotiation process. Russia's delegation chief Vladimir Medinsky has questioned the inclusion of European countries in the peace talks, suggesting that their input is unclear and lacking concrete proposals. Russia's foreign policy goal is reportedly focused on creating a new, modern Yalta", according to Medinsky's statement to Russian TV, implying a significant shift in the country's stance on international relations. In related developments, Kushner has expressed his intention to discuss ways to involve European countries more directly in the peace talks with Putin. This move aims to address concerns that Europe's input is unclear and lacks concrete proposals. The involvement of top officials from major Western powers would undoubtedly add weight to the negotiations. As part of a broader effort to foster international cooperation, senior diplomats from Britain, France, Germany, Italy, NATO, and the European Union have converged on Abu Dhabi for high-level meetings. These talks are likely to focus on finding common ground between Ukraine, Russia, and their respective allies in Europe and North America. The ongoing conflict has left a devastating trail of destruction, with hundreds of thousands killed since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022. Millions more have been displaced by the relentless aerial bombardments that have ravaged large areas of eastern and southern Ukraine. articles.summary: The 1994 Saab 900 SE Coupe that once belonged to John F. Kennedy Jr. is currently up for auction via RR Auction.
articles.content: A rare opportunity has arisen for car enthusiasts and fans of John F. Kennedy Jr. alike, as his 1994 Saab 900 SE Coupe is currently up for auction via RR Auction. This unique vehicle reflects the eclectic style that characterized JFK Jr.'s approach to fashion and lifestyle in 1990s New York. The Saab 900 was a quintessential representation of the era's quirky aesthetic, with its hunter green paint job standing out as a testament to JFK Jr.'s bold taste. This Swedish sports car embodied the perfect blend of sportiness and sophistication, making it a fitting choice for someone who didn't conform to traditional style norms. The auction has already generated significant interest, with bids rolling in from around the world. For those who admire JFK Jr.'s unique sense of style and are looking to own a piece of automotive history, this is an opportunity not to be missed, the sale will give one lucky buyer the chance to drive away in a truly one-of-a-kind vehicle. The 1994 Saab has become an iconic symbol of '90s culture, known for its unique blend of Scandinavian design and postmodern flair. Its distinctive features, such as the ignition being located next to the handbrake, made it a favorite among style-conscious Americans who appreciated its understated yet sophisticated aesthetic. Saabs were also a staple in popular culture during this time period, with notable figures like Jerry Seinfeld's TV alter-ego and characters from National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation frequently depicted driving one. The car's blend of aristocratic, athletic, and bohemian elements was particularly appealing to those who valued individuality and self-expression. This 1994 Saab is significant not only because of its association with '90s culture but also due to its connection to the late John F. Kennedy Jr. and his wife Carolyn Bessette Kennedy. According to Bobby Livingston, executive vice president at RR Auction, this car stands out from more flashy luxury vehicles because it was a practical part of JFK Jr.'s everyday life. The 1994 Saab that once belonged to John F. Kennedy Jr. has been consigned for sale via Kevin J. Hynes, a screenwriter and close friend of the late pilot. According to auction records, Hynes acquired the car from the Kennedy estate in 2000 for $6,000. It's reported that the Saab was left at Hynes' Westchester home after Kennedy's fatal plane crash in 1999. The vehicle had been a part of Kennedy's daily life since he purchased it in the summer of 1994 and drove it until his death. The car's third owner is said to have started the engine regularly, but its low mileage of just 30,650 miles suggests that it has not been driven extensively in recent years. This Saab will be sold through RR Auction as part of a larger sale featuring various autographed items and artifacts. As part of this auction, which also includes a tweed hat once worn by President John F. Kennedy's father, the minimum price for bidding on the Saab is set at $15,000. The auction for JFK Jr.'s 1994 Saab has attracted significant interest, with over 20 bids driving the price close to $30,000 by Wednesday afternoon. According to a spokesperson, the strong bidding is not surprising given the car's unique provenance and its status as a piece of automotive history. The sale of other celebrity-owned vehicles, such as Tupac's Hummer and Tony Soprano's Cadillac Escalade, has also hinted at a growing demand for these types of items. The 1994 Saab is poised to end up with a car collector or someone who can appreciate its value as a piece of '90s style iconography. Whoever purchases the vehicle would do well to give it the care and attention it deserves to maintain its status as a nostalgic treasure. articles.summary: The use of OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol model has enabled the programming of a virtual robot to interact with its environment and perform specific tasks.
articles.content: A breakthrough in robotics has been achieved through the use of OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol model, which enables the programming of a virtual robot to interact with its environment and perform specific tasks. I've successfully trained a digital version of Microduck, a cute robotic companion developed by Pollen Robotics and Hugging Face, to navigate around a room and detect the presence of a Bengal cat. The ease with which I was able to code and train the virtual robot in just a few hours is a testament to the power of OpenAI's latest models. This is a significant improvement over previous methods, which could take weeks or even months to accomplish. The GPT-6 Sol model has made it possible for developers to understand and manipulate 3D representations of the physical world, allowing them to translate this knowledge into practical code and robotic actions. The potential applications of this technology are vast, and real-world roboticists are already exploring its possibilities. Professor Ken Goldberg from the University of California, Berkeley, and his students were among those who saw demos showcasing the capabilities of OpenAI's Astra model when it was released in September. They witnessed how it could render 3D images with remarkable accuracy. This development has significant implications for the field of robotics, where programming and training robots to interact with their environment can be a time-consuming and complex process. With the help of OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol model, roboticists may soon be able to create more sophisticated and autonomous machines that can perform tasks with greater ease and efficiency. Researchers are exploring new ways to train robots using simulations, which require immense detail and accuracy to ensure successful transfer to real-world applications. To create realistic simulations, roboticists need vast amounts of data and precise control over various parameters such as camera position, lighting, and background settings. This process can be time-consuming and labor-intensive, but Astra's capabilities are changing that. Astra was given access to an Nvidia tool called Newton, which allows it to generate detailed 3D simulations quickly and accurately. In one instance, Astra created a simulation of a real robot scene in just under an hour, complete with precise settings for camera placement, lighting, and materials. By automating tasks such as running experiments and analyzing results, Astra is making the training process more efficient and less prone to human error. The latest advancements in robotics have made significant strides in automating tasks and reducing human error. By using OpenAI's newest model in conjunction with Nvidia's Isaac Sim software, researchers are able to remotely control virtual robots and fine-tune their training regimes. This innovative approach allows for a more efficient and streamlined process of configuring and programming physical robots. The model can feed instructions to the virtual robot, observe its actions, and suggest improvements to its training regimen. This level of automation has made it possible to achieve complex tasks, such as getting a virtual duck to walk around without toppling over. The integration of AI models with robotics has also led to new ways of thinking about control systems. According to Jim Fan, a researcher at Nvidia, the ability to control robots using AI mirrors how software agents function on computers. This means that models trained to perform physical actions can be accessed and utilized just like different software programs. Researchers are now exploring the capabilities of visual language action (VLA) models in controlling physical actions. These models have the potential to revolutionize robotics by enabling seamless interaction between humans, AI, and robots. As researchers continue to push the boundaries of robotics, they're making rapid progress in developing robots that can learn and adapt like humans. A key innovation is the Aspire framework, an open-source initiative that allows robots to discover new skills on their own. One example of this capability was showcased by GPT-6 Astra, which demonstrated its ability to solve a Rubik's cube using a pair of robot arms. The process wasn't seamless, however - the robot initially struggled with the angle and technique required to twist the cube's pieces into place. This challenge highlights one of the significant hurdles in robotics development: creating robots that can perform complex tasks without requiring extensive engineering expertise. However, researchers are optimistic about their progress, particularly with regards to enabling robots to learn from experience and adapt to new situations. The potential for robots to automate routine tasks has also been demonstrated through a painting exercise conducted by Fan at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas. In this demo, GPT-6 Astra was tasked with creating a picture of the Golden Gate Bridge using nearby paint and brushes - and it successfully completed the task. The potential applications of GPT-6 Astra's capabilities extend far beyond creative tasks, as it has the potential to revolutionize industries such as manufacturing and e-commerce. Several industrial robotics and automation firms have already expressed interest in this approach, which could lead to significant advancements in efficiency and productivity. With the ease of training robots using AI, hobbyists and engineers may soon experience breakthroughs in "vibe robotics," much like the impact of vibe coding a few years ago. This could enable more people to explore and develop their own robotic creations, further accelerating innovation in this field. articles.title: Aurel Bacs Partners With Vacheron Constantin For Historic Watch Competition
articles.summary: The competition, which featured 550 entries from around the world, was won by historic watches evaluated based on beauty and historical significance.
articles.content: A pioneering event in the world of horology has taken place in Geneva, marking a significant milestone for collectors of vintage timepieces. The competition, which pitted historic watches against each other, was the brainchild of renowned auctioneer Aurel Bacs and his team at Phillips. In a rare instance of collaboration between industry heavyweights, Bacs partnered with Swiss luxury watchmaker Vacheron Constantin to make this unique event a reality. Contrary to what one might expect from an automotive Concours d'Elegance, the focus was not on speed or performance but rather on aesthetic appeal. A panel of 14 expert judges, including Bacs himself, Hodinkee's Ben Clymer, and watch journalist Roberta Naas, carefully evaluated each submission based on its beauty and historical significance. The response to this inaugural competition was overwhelming, with a staggering 550 entries submitted from around the world. This forced the organizers to narrow down their selection to just 34 finalist watches, whose owners were flown in for the event at the Hôtel Président in Geneva. The evening drew a crowd of approximately 200 attendees, all gathered to witness this historic occasion. Aurel Bacs expressed his enthusiasm and pride over the success of this first-ever timepiece competition, describing it as "the most beautiful evening in the field ever." This event has set a new standard for watch collectors and enthusiasts alike, providing a unique platform for owners of rare and exquisite timepieces to showcase their treasures. The competition's sheer scale and prestige have undoubtedly raised the bar for future events. As the world of horology continues to evolve, this pioneering initiative is poised to inspire a new generation of collectors and connoisseurs. The competition's rigorous judging process involved evaluating watches based on nine criteria, including authenticity, elegance, and rarity, as well as their impact on Vacheron Constantin's history and watchmaking in general. Each category had its own set of contenders, with the jurors deliberating for several hours to select the winners. The results were finally announced at a gathering on the lower floor of the Hôtel Président, where a cocktail reception had taken place earlier. The Chronographs category featured a range of historic timepieces, including a highly rare ref. 4072 in stainless steel from 1940. However, it was a yellow gold pocket-watch chronograph from 1929 that emerged as the winner, surprising many in attendance with its unexpected victory. This particular watch's win sparked a collective gasp from the audience, comprised of watch enthusiasts familiar with the historical significance of pocket watches. The pocket-watch chronograph's triumph raised questions about whether these traditional timepieces could regain their former status as the pinnacle of watch collecting. The winning piece was described as being in excellent condition, featuring a white enamel dial with dual registers in an "up-down configuration. Its beauty and craftsmanship were widely admired by those present, including its intricate details and precise mechanics. The pocket watch's intricate details and precise mechanics were overshadowed by another stunning timepiece. A blue sapphire-encrusted pocket watch took top honors, its beauty and craftsmanship captivating the audience. Its owner, an American gentleman, revealed a remarkable history for the winning watch, which had once belonged to His Majesty Alexander I of Yugoslavia. The king had given it to Dr. Otto von Frangeš, who wore it during a pivotal moment in history - sitting in the motorcade when the king was assassinated in France in 1934. This pocket watch's journey didn't end there; it would later be smuggled out of Yugoslavia by Dr. Frangeš's son Nikola, hidden inside his wife's jacket as they escaped the Iron Curtain in the late 1940s. The Chronomètre Royal sub-brand was specifically designed for life at sea, with parts resistant to magnetism and rust. Launched by Vacheron in 1907, this line prioritized precision timing, which was crucial for maritime navigation. The intricacies of vintage timepieces were on full display as a unique platinum-cased watch from 1957 took top honors in a recent competition. This Cioccolatone was owned by an Italian collector who beamed with pride as he accepted the award alongside his grown son, showcasing the timepiece's exceptional design and craftsmanship. The winning watch boasted a complete calendar feature, adding to its already impressive list of complications. Housed in a 34mm x 43mm rectangular case, it demonstrated Vacheron's mastery of precision timing, a skill honed over decades of innovation. In contrast, other contenders included more modern pieces like the skeletonized QP wristwatch from 1987, which also made it to the final round. However, the Cioccolatone" stood out for its rarity and uniqueness. Multiple Complications proved to be a strong suit for Vacheron, with one of their watches boasting an impressive array of complications, including minute repeater, day, and retrograde date indications. This diminutive yellow-gold timepiece was once considered the world's most complicated wristwatch when it was delivered in 1940. A time-only ref. 4695 dress watch stood out among the competition for its intricate lugs and Maltese Cross-type dial. This particular model was notable for its unique design features that set it apart from other watches of its kind. Its presence at the competition added to the diversity of entries. The winner in one category, however, took everyone by surprise. It belonged to a tall Italian gentleman who had previously owned another highly sought-after timepiece. The new watch, an automatic world timer made of yellow gold, was produced in 1957 and featured Louis Cottier's system, which is extremely rare even among collectors. The competition's Best of Show award went to a platinum wristwatch with diamond-set indices, a seemingly simple time-only dress watch that belies its intricate hand-wound movement. The 13-ligne minute-repeater mechanism is a rare feature, especially in this particular example which was produced in only three instances in the early 1960s. Its brushed-finish case and teardrop lugs make it a unique piece. This platinum timepiece is not only exceptional due to its rarity but also because it marks the last minute-repeating reference from the brand for nearly 30 years. The crowd at the awards ceremony was moved by the stories shared by each watch owner about their timepieces, highlighting the emotional connection people have with these historic and vintage watches. The event's format is expected to be repeated in the future. The first concours for watches has sparked interest among collectors and brands alike, with potential for either Vacheron to continue hosting it or other brands to adopt a similar format. Alternatively, the competition might evolve into a more traditional multi-brand event like the Concours d’Élégance at Pebble Beach, but its success is certain to be repeated in some form. The communication breakdown between Norfolk State's head coach and his offensive coordinator has been a topic of discussion after their recent game. He wanted to go into victory formation immediately, as there were no timeouts left for the opposing team. The opposing team would have needed to cover 80 yards in just 18 seconds if they had managed to get the ball back, making it highly unlikely that they could score. However, the coordinator's plan was not communicated effectively to the coach, leading to a misalignment of their strategies. This lack of coordination ultimately led to the blunder. The head coach has taken responsibility for the mistake, acknowledging that he should have clearly conveyed his intentions to the coordinator. He emphasized that as the head coach, it is his duty to see through the game until the final whistle blows. The blame lies with him, not with the coordinator, who was simply following his own instincts. The head coach has also highlighted the importance of clear communication between coaches and players during critical moments in a game. He acknowledged that what he should have done was explicitly tell the coordinator to go into victory formation, ensuring that everyone is on the same page. Michael Vick, head coach of Norfolk State University's football team, acknowledged that his reaction after a recent game was misplaced. He expressed regret for his emotional outburst and praised his coordinator's play-calling skills. Vick also reflected on the events leading up to his mistake, stating that while he thought the game was over, others on the team were still considering different scenarios. This showed a level of maturity and understanding from the players, which Vick acknowledged as fair. Ultimately, Vick took full responsibility for the blunder, recognizing that it was his duty as head coach to be aware of all situations and make informed decisions. articles.content: Ciryl Gane is set to make his first full title defense against Josh Hokit at UFC 334 on Saturday at Madison Square Garden in New York. articles.title: Bill Aims to Prevent Pardon Abuse in Trump Administration

articles.content: Congressional Democrats have introduced a bill aimed at tackling what they call the pardon industrial complex - a system where wealthy individuals can allegedly purchase pardons for themselves or others. The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act seeks to prevent acts of clemency that raise potential conflicts of interest or involve favors for President Trump's allies and donors. According to Rep. Mike Levin, one of the bill's co-authors, America has become a place where "you literally, for the highest dollar amount, can go and buy a pardon". This assertion suggests that the pardon process has been compromised by financial influence. The Founders' original intention was not for pardons to be bought or sold, Levin emphasized. The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act is unlikely to pass without facing Mr. Trump's veto, but its introduction offers insight into how Democrats plan to utilize their new majorities in Congress to scrutinize President Trump's use of the pardon power. Wealthy defendants have been using lobbyists and lawyers tied to President Trump to influence their pardon cases at the White House. According to data, nearly 70% of his second-term clemency actions have bypassed the Justice Department's pardon office, a figure that rises to 92% when including January. This has led lawmakers to scrutinize the president's use of the pardon power. The bill proposed by Democrats would direct the Justice Department's inspector general to investigate pardons that raise potential conflicts of interest. As examples of such cases, lawmakers pointed to President Trump's pardon of Changpeng Zhao, a cryptocurrency founder who pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to maintain an effective anti-money-laundering program. The White House has maintained that its pardon review process is robust and includes input from various officials, including White House counsel, the Justice Department, and "pardon czar Alice Johnson. However, reports have raised questions about potential conflicts of interest, such as the case of Alina Habba Mildon, a former Justice Department adviser who struck a deal with the family of a Venezuelan billionaire just before he was pardoned. The proposed legislation aims to curb potential abuse of presidential pardons by introducing stricter guidelines and accountability measures. Specifically, it would clarify that the president and vice president can be held liable for trading pardons in exchange for something of value. In addition to these provisions, the bill would also require individuals receiving pardons to disclose any gifts they receive related to presidential projects, such as libraries or White House facilities. The proposed ban on self-pardons is another key aspect of the legislation, which has sparked debate about its implications. The proposed legislation aims to curb what some have dubbed the pardon industrial complex", a phenomenon where presidential pardons are granted in exchange for personal or financial gain. Supporters of the ban argue that it will help prevent abuse of the pardon power, while critics warn of unintended constitutional consequences and potential backlashes on future administrations. articles.title: Nvidia's Founder Faces Scrutiny Over Alleged Conflicts of Interest
articles.summary: The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence believed Alice Huang was a Chinese asset, raising questions about Nvidia's governance and oversight.
articles.content: Nvidia's founder and CEO Jensen Huang is widely regarded as a visionary leader who has revolutionized the tech industry with his groundbreaking innovations. His influence extends far beyond the company he founded, with many CEOs around the world admiring his entrepreneurial spirit and bold vision for the future. However, recent events have raised concerns about Huang's leadership and potential conflicts of interest. Amidst calls for his resignation from some top GOP voices, including Sen. Kevin Cramer of the Senate Banking Committee, questions are being asked about how Nvidia's board allowed these issues to go unchecked. In October 2025, a report by the New York Times revealed that Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company, had purchased billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips amid suspicions that it was helping China evade U.S. restrictions on chip exports. Nvidia initially claimed that an internal review found no evidence of its chips being diverted to China. However, this assertion was later challenged by Culper Research, a short seller, which alleged "uncomfortably close ties" between Alice Huang, the head of Megaspeed, and Jensen Huang in May 2026. Despite these allegations, Nvidia's board seemed content to leave the matter unresolved. The situation took a further turn last month when the New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence believed Alice Huang was a Chinese asset. A company spokesperson attempted to downplay the claims, stating that the diversion allegations had been debunked and describing the relationship as normal. This response has sparked widespread criticism, with many questioning why Nvidia's board failed to investigate these allegations more thoroughly. The situation is further complicated by Jensen Huang's admission last month that he had been unfaithful to his wife in a message referencing national security concerns in the press. The sequence of events raises serious questions about the governance and oversight at Nvidia. It also highlights the need for greater transparency and accountability within companies, particularly those with significant influence over global technology markets. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how Nvidia's board will respond to these allegations and whether any further action will be taken against Jensen Huang or other company officials. The Caremark doctrine, established in 1996 in Delaware Chancery Court, sets a high standard for corporate directors to monitor risks central to their business and take action when they become aware of potential issues. Under this doctrine, several boards have faced trouble in Delaware Chancery Court for failing to oversee key areas of their operations. For instance, the directors of Blue Bell Creameries were sued over their lack of oversight on food safety before a deadly listeria outbreak in 2019. The case against Boeing's directors is another example of the consequences of neglecting critical risks. The board had no committee responsible for airplane safety, which contributed to the 737 MAX crashes. The lawsuit was eventually settled for $237.5 million. In both cases, the courts emphasized that boards must take an active role in monitoring potential risks, rather than relying solely on management's judgment. This means directors cannot simply trust their executives to handle critical issues, even if those risks were unforeseeable or unanticipated. Now, Nvidia's board will face scrutiny over its handling of Megaspeed, a high-speed interconnect technology that has been at the center of controversy. Plaintiffs' lawyers will likely ask questions about who conducted reviews on Megaspeed and whether they reported to independent directors or management. The answers to these questions are recorded in the board meeting minutes, which can be accessed with relative ease by shareholders due to a Delaware law that allows for transparency in such matters. This is particularly relevant for Nvidia, as the company has a history of fighting to keep its records private. Nvidia's experience in battling books-and-records demands may ultimately prove beneficial to plaintiffs, who will use this access to build their case against the board. Nvidia's management conflict of interest is a significant concern that the board should have addressed. A Megaspeed affiliate purchased approximately $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia-powered equipment in just two years, raising questions about the company's compliance record. This large customer relationship also created an apparent conflict of interest for Jensen Huang, who has a personal tie to an executive at Megaspeed. According to Nvidia's own code of conduct, this type of relationship would likely require disclosure. The board should have been vigilant in monitoring potential management conflicts and ensuring that they do not compromise the company's compliance record. However, when questions first arose about Megaspeed's dealings with Nvidia, the company provided assurances from individuals who report directly to Huang, potentially creating a conflict of interest in their own testimony. Nvidia's general counsel went so far as to contact a senior Commerce Department official regarding the government's investigation into Megaspeed. It is unclear whether the board authorized this call or was even aware of it. This raises questions about the board's oversight and ability to ensure that the company is complying with relevant laws and regulations. The stakes are high for Nvidia, given its production of strategically sensitive products. The Information reported that companies tied to Alice Huang helped Chinese buyers obtain $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips, including banned ones laundered through neutral parties. While Megaspeed denies any wrongdoing, the potential consequences of export violations are severe and should have prompted more thorough investigation by the board. Nvidia's own proxy statement reveals a concerning lack of oversight in trade compliance. The company's committee responsible for trade compliance met only three times last fiscal year, and there is no chief compliance officer on staff. This raises questions about how much the board knew and when they became aware of potential issues. The board's failure to address these concerns may ultimately lead to shareholder lawsuits in Delaware Chancery Court. As Nvidia battles allegations of export control evasion and management conflicts, its experience in battling books-and-records demands will likely be crucial in building a case against the board. The allegations of export control evasion and management conflicts at Nvidia have raised concerns about the company's national security risks. US officials reportedly concluded that Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gain access to Jensen Huang and influence his views on chip sales to China. Jensen Huang has been a vocal advocate for continuing to sell chips to China, arguing that it would prevent the country from developing its own semiconductor industry. This stance is at odds with concerns raised by some US officials about the potential national security risks of selling advanced technology to China. The president was briefed on the matter in late 2025 and a secret memo circulated among policymakers earlier this year, around the same time Jensen Huang was appointed to the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. Three House committee chairmen have now requested a closed-door briefing with Jensen Huang, while the president has said that the FBI is reviewing the matter. The Nvidia board's lack of national security expertise raises questions about their diligence in addressing these risks. None of the directors have a background in this area, which could be crucial for making informed decisions. With no one on the board having experience in national security, it is unclear what steps were taken to mitigate potential risks or whether they even asked management about the matter. The Nvidia board's failure to address Jensen Huang's lack of a clear successor has left the company vulnerable to potential risks. With over 50 direct reports, it is concerning that there is no identified individual to take over in his absence. This oversight raises questions about the board's diligence in ensuring a smooth transition. A prominent analyst estimates that Nvidia would be worth significantly less without Jensen Huang at the helm, suggesting that his departure could have severe financial consequences for the company. This assessment underscores the importance of having a clear succession plan in place to mitigate potential risks. The board's apparent idolatry of Jensen Huang has created an environment where it seems impossible for anyone else to step into leadership. This lack of diversity and perspective within the executive team is concerning, particularly given the significant responsibilities that come with leading a company like Nvidia. In light of these concerns, it is surprising that the board did not prioritize succession planning until it became a pressing issue. By failing to address this critical matter, they have put the entire organization at risk. The absence of a clear plan has left Nvidia exposed to potential disruptions and instability. The board's statement announcing its investigation into Jensen Huang's dealings seems to be more about reassuring investors than conducting a thorough inquiry. By declaring confidence in Jensen before even beginning the investigation, it raises questions about their impartiality and commitment to uncovering the truth. As experts in corporate governance, we have extensively studied instances where dual-class shares have been used effectively to protect founder control and facilitate long-term investment. Companies like Berkshire Hathaway, Alphabet, and The New York Times are notable examples of successful dual-class share structures that have allowed founders or families to maintain control while investing for the future. Our research has shown that when implemented correctly, dual-class shares can be a valuable tool for companies seeking to balance short-term pressures with long-term goals. However, it is essential to recognize that these structures must be carefully designed and managed to avoid potential pitfalls and ensure equitable treatment of all shareholders. The Nvidia board's failure to provide effective oversight was not due to the company's capital structure, which is surprisingly shareholder-friendly. Despite having a single class of common stock and a declassified board, Jensen Huang has managed to maintain an unprecedented level of control. Jensen owns just 3.5% of the company's shares, but he casts 3.5% of the votes, giving him significant influence over the board. However, this is not unusual in itself - what is remarkable is that no CEO in America has been as immune to scrutiny and oversight as Jensen Huang. The Nvidia board's apparent idolatry of Jensen Huang is a key factor in his entrenched position. Despite his impressive track record of building the company from humble beginnings, the directors seem to have become too enamored with him to provide proper oversight. This social and interpersonal connection between the board and Jensen has led to a lack of scrutiny and oversight that is unusual even by corporate standards. No charter provision or proxy adviser would have flagged this issue, highlighting the complexity of the problem. In contrast, critics often point to dual-class shares as the root cause of entrenched founder control, but Nvidia's single share class makes it clear that other factors are at play. The company's independent majority, lead director, and annual elections all suggest a level of transparency and accountability that is rare in corporate governance. Ultimately, the Nvidia board's failure to provide effective oversight has left shareholders vulnerable to potential lawsuits, highlighting the importance of careful board design and management to avoid similar pitfalls in the future. As the integration of AI assistants in in-car software continues to evolve, Google's decision to bring Gemini Intelligence to Android Auto marks an important step forward in enhancing the user experience on the road. articles.title: Cyberattack on French Supermarkets Causes Massive Food Spoilage
articles.summary: A recent wave of hacks has compromised key sectors in France, with hundreds of supermarkets affected by a cyberattack that caused food spoilage.
articles.content: France has emerged as a prime target for cyberattacks in Europe, according to some analysts who point to a recent wave of major hacks that have compromised several key sectors. A particularly brazen incident occurred on October 12 when hundreds of supermarket workers in France discovered that their refrigerators and freezers had been hacked. Instead of being chilled, the equipment was emitting scorching hot air, rendering the stored food useless. This hack affected an estimated 700 stores across the country, with temperature-control software exploited to crank up the thermostats as high as 80°C (176°F) overnight in some cases. The result was a massive loss of perishable goods, with tonnes of spoiled food discarded by workers at various supermarket chains. The hack marked "the first large-scale cyberattack aimed at sabotage" on French territory, according to Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, who described the incident as an attack of "unprecedented scale. This high-profile breach has added to a growing list of major cyberattacks that have hit France in recent years. These incidents include successful hacks targeting various government departments and public service providers, including the country's unemployment agency, immigration office, ministry of education, national agency for identity documents, and public hospitals, all within the past five years. The French government has been hit by a significant data breach in recent months, affecting nearly 680,000 taxpayers who had their personal and tax information stolen and put up for sale online. In addition to these high-profile hacks targeting the government, numerous French companies have also fallen victim to large-scale data theft. This includes major health insurers, banks, retail chains, mobile phone providers, and even the national airline AirFrance-KLM. French companies have been hit hard by cyberattacks, with many suffering significant losses due to stolen customer data. The frequency and scale of these attacks have earned France a reputation as the most heavily breached large jurisdiction in Europe", according to cybersecurity firm UpGuard. Experts point to several factors that make France an attractive target for hackers. As the country's economy is one of the largest in Europe, it offers a rich source of valuable data and financial information. France's attribution of October's supermarket hack to an Iranian cyber unit affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards highlights a rare instance of state-linked hacking in the country. This type of high-profile attack is distinct from the everyday threats faced by European organisations, such as ransomware, data theft, and fraud. In November, French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa suffered a significant loss when cybercriminals stole more than €100 million, demonstrating that France is not immune to these types of attacks. The layered appeal of targeting France may bring hackers together to collaborate on sophisticated attacks, increasing their chances of success. France's cyberattack woes may be partly due to its reputation as a target of choice for hackers, but it is not the only European country facing a significant threat. In fact, Germany and Italy have been listed by ransomware groups more frequently than France over the past year, according to cybersecurity experts. This suggests that other countries in Europe are also vulnerable to cyberattacks. Meanwhile, Ukraine has emerged as the European country where customers are most often impacted by cyber threats, according to Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defence Report. The report highlights the need for enhanced cybersecurity measures across the continent. The threat of cyberattacks is not limited to France or even Europe. A large-scale attack on Poland's energy grid in December 2025 was attributed to Russia and prompted the EU and UK to impose their first joint cyber sanctions. Cybersecurity experts warn that France's industrial control systems are particularly vulnerable, with thousands of insecure systems throughout the EU waiting to be exploited by hackers. France's industrial control systems are particularly vulnerable to cyberattacks due to outdated services and zero-day vulnerabilities. Many of these vulnerabilities can be attributed to third-party suppliers, such as Danish engineering firm Danfoss, which provided refrigeration management systems to France's hacked supermarkets. Danfoss has pointed out that most of the attacks targeted products that no longer receive software or security updates. The company advises its customers to keep their systems and products updated to prevent similar breaches in the future. This recommendation is crucial for companies and public authorities looking to avoid falling prey to cyberattacks. The ease with which these vulnerabilities can be exploited has led cybersecurity experts to warn about the importance of basic cybersecurity measures. Kipker notes that many organisations are successfully attacked not because they have been specifically targeted, but due to a lack of robust security protocols in place. To mitigate the increasing number of cyberattacks in France, it's essential for the country to accelerate its efforts in cybersecurity. The EU's cybersecurity chief has recently highlighted that even home appliances could be vulnerable to attacks, following the recent hacking incidents involving refrigerators and other smart devices. This warning underscores the growing threat posed by advanced technologies used by hackers to scale up their operations. Despite the escalating security challenges, experts emphasize that good cyber hygiene practices can still prevent a significant amount of opportunistic cybercrime, making it crucial for individuals and organizations alike to adopt robust security protocols. articles.title: Machu Picchu Weather Factors Influence Travel Planning
articles.summary: Visitors to Machu Picchu must balance clear views with smaller crowds due to varying weather conditions.
articles.content: Visitors planning a trip to Machu Picchu often have a clear idea of what they want to see and experience before even booking their travel dates. However, the massive scale and intricate stone walls of the Inca city demand time to take in and appreciate fully, making it essential to allocate sufficient time for exploration. But there's another crucial factor to consider: the weather. A single bank of cloud can obscure Waynapicchu, the peak behind the ruins, and with it the breathtaking panorama that draws visitors from around the globe. While the drier months may offer better odds of clear views, they also coincide with peak tourist season, resulting in larger crowds and longer lines at popular entry points. On the other hand, the weeks immediately following the rainy season often bring lush greenery to the slopes and a welcome respite from the crowds that flock to Machu Picchu during its dry winter months. To make the most of their visit, first-time travelers must weigh their priorities: do they crave clear views or prefer smaller crowds? The answer will determine the best time for them to arrive in this Andean wonderland. The route calendar plays a significant role in planning a trip to Machu Picchu, particularly for those hoping to walk to the Sun Gate or Inca Bridge. The shoulder season in Machu Picchu offers a unique advantage for travelers who can tolerate some rain and mist. Alice Farkas, marketing and communications lead at Aracari, suggests that April is an excellent time to visit, with fewer tourists yet still pleasant weather. Kiernan Cochran from Andean, which plans trips throughout Peru, agrees that the early part of May is also a good option for those who prefer drier conditions. However, Cochran notes that popular routes tend to fill up quickly, requiring similar lead times as high season. Visiting Machu Picchu during the off-season, November through March, can result in significant savings on airfare and accommodations. Yet, strategic planning is crucial during this period, particularly when it comes to permits for popular routes like Huayna Picchu, which still require three-month advance booking. The rainy season has its own charm, as expert guides point out that the rain mainly falls at night, rather than throughout the day. The ticket system at Machu Picchu is complex and divided into various categories based on route and entry time. Visitors should be aware that even if there is overall availability for tickets, their preferred route and entry time may still be full due to the specific allocation process. To increase chances of securing a spot on popular routes, travelers are advised to book about six months in advance during peak season and at least three months ahead during off-peak periods. Given the importance of planning ahead when visiting Machu Picchu, it's essential for first-time visitors to allocate sufficient time to explore the region. A recommended duration for exploring the area is four or five nights, which allows for a gentle acclimatization process and a more leisurely pace. The Sacred Valley serves as an ideal starting point, providing an introduction to the Inca culture that built Machu Picchu through its well-preserved towns and terraces. Cusco, situated at approximately 11,150 feet above sea level, is where flights currently land, but travelers can opt to head straight down to the Sacred Valley for a gentler start. Before arriving at Machu Picchu, it's essential to choose the right route for your visit, as each one offers a unique perspective on this ancient Inca site. The official route maps divide the site into three circuits: Classic Circuit 1, Classic Circuit 2, and the lower royal sector circuit. Each circuit has its own routes that cater to different interests and physical abilities. When deciding which route to book, consider your priorities - do you want to witness the breathtaking upper-terrace panorama or explore the Inca buildings of the urban sector? The Classic Circuit 2 is recommended for a single visit, as it pairs a viewpoint with a walk among the Inca ruins. Route 2-B takes its view from the lower terrace, which may be worth knowing if you have a specific camera angle in mind. On the other hand, route 1-B offers an upper-terrace panorama while keeping you above the main streets. For those who want to experience the classic view down onto the site, Circuit 1's route 1-A adds the climb up Machu Picchu Mountain. Meanwhile, the Sun Gate and Inca Bridge carry seasonal tickets of their own, requiring separate permits. Circuit 3 covers the lower royal sector, including the Temple of the Sun. If you're interested in exploring this area, consider booking Circuit 3 separately, as it offers a unique perspective on the site's history. If your preferred route sells out, Andean recommends booking Circuits 1 and 3 separately to combine the panorama with a closer look at the ruins. However, be aware that tickets cannot be switched to another route once you arrive at Machu Picchu. When purchasing tickets for Machu Picchu, it's essential to understand what's included in your hike before buying additional admission. Under new rules introduced in September 2026, trail arrivals enter on a designated Circuit 3-B ticket, which has implications if you also want to visit Circuit 2 or the upper panorama. Heavy rainfall can disrupt access to the kilometer 104 path outside of the usual February maintenance period, making it crucial to consider weather conditions during rainy season travel. To secure entry to Machu Picchu, tickets must be purchased through the Ministry of Culture's online portal, Tu Boleto. When buying tickets, visitors are required to enter their details carefully, matching names and information to the same identification document they'll present at the gate. Travelers to Machu Picchu typically begin their journey in Cusco, where they can board a train from Ollantaytambo in the Sacred Valley for the ride along the Urubamba River to Machu Picchu Pueblo. From there, a separate shuttle bus takes passengers up to the entrance of the site, a trip that usually lasts around half an hour. When planning their travel arrangements, visitors should check the boarding points and total travel time before choosing a fare, as some departures from Cusco may involve a bus-and-train transfer during certain periods. For first-time visitors, arriving by morning train from the Sacred Valley and entering the site in the afternoon can be a good strategy for avoiding crowds; typically, three or four hours is sufficient to explore the area. Among the premium trains available are options like Belmond's Hiram Bingham, PeruRail's Vistadome Observatory, and IncaRail's First Class. articles.title: Hotel California handwritten lyrics play key role in Manhattan trial collapse
articles.summary: A 2012 discovery led Don Henley to track down his missing handwritten lyrics, which had been used as evidence in a Manhattan case.
articles.content: The Eagles' iconic album Hotel California turns 50 this December, a milestone marking one of the biggest albums of 1976. However, the creation of this musical masterpiece involved more than just music - it also led to a surprising turn of events in a Manhattan criminal case. Before Don Henley and his bandmates began recording their songs, they jotted down lyrics on legal pads purchased at a Los Angeles stationery store. Roughly 100 of these handwritten pages played a central role in the collapsed trial, leaving many wondering how such an unusual connection came to be. The Eagles had authorized Ed Sanders to write their biography in 1979 under a contract that granted him access to exclusive material. In exchange for this privilege, the band stipulated that any provided content would remain its sole property. Don Henley allowed Sanders to sift through his handwritten lyric drafts as part of the research process. This decision to share his work led to the pages ending up in the wrong hands, ultimately becoming a crucial piece of evidence in the Manhattan criminal case. The trial's abrupt collapse raises questions about how these sensitive documents were used and whether the band's intentions had been compromised. The trial's outcome is just one aspect of this unusual story, which continues to unfold as we explore the circumstances surrounding Don Henley's handwritten lyrics for Hotel California. The handwritten lyrics to Don Henley's iconic song "Hotel California have a history that predates their recent trial. The pages had been misplaced for years, and it wasn't until they surfaced in 2012 that Henley was able to track them down. When the pages were eventually found, they had changed hands several times. They had first been sold by a former songwriter's assistant to rare-book dealer Glenn Horowitz around 2005. From there, they made their way to former Rock & Roll Hall of Fame curator Craig Inciardi and memorabilia auctioneer Edward Kosinski. The trail of ownership was complicated, with the pages being passed from one collector to another. It wasn't until Henley saw them for sale that he realized what had happened to his original work. He eventually purchased some of the sheets back from Kosinski in April 2012 for $8,500. As it turned out, Henley's recollection of where the pages came from was shrouded in uncertainty. Over the years, he gave different accounts to Horowitz about how they had originated. In one instance, he claimed his assistant had sent them from Malibu; on another occasion, he said he'd found them discarded in a backstage dressing room. The discrepancies in Henley's story only added to the confusion surrounding the missing pages. His memories were indeed foggy, as he himself acknowledged in 2012 when trying to explain what had happened to his work. As the case against the defendants continues, it remains to be seen how this complex history will play out in court. The trial has shed light on the intricate web of ownership and the often murky world of rare collectibles. The investigation into the authenticity of Don Henley's handwritten Hotel California lyrics has revealed a complex web of ownership and potential deception. According to testimony, the writer of the manuscript had provided multiple explanations for its origins over the years, including claims that it was sent from Malibu by Henley's assistant or found in a backstage dressing room. These accounts were made in various forms, with one written statement from 2012 citing foggy memory as a reason for the inconsistencies. The writer had also been asked to provide further information about the manuscript's origins. In 2017, Horowitz asked the writer if the pages came from Frey, who had passed away the previous year. This inquiry was made with the involvement of Henley's lawyers and the Manhattan District Attorney's office. Horowitz's follow-up message reportedly stated that identifying Frey as the source of the manuscript would be sufficient to resolve the matter for all parties involved. The trial against three men accused of conspiring to keep and sell handwritten lyrics from Don Henley's song Hotel California continued in February 2024 before Judge Curtis Farber. Prosecutors valued the stolen pages at over $1 million, despite none of the defendants being accused of theft. Instead, they were charged with concealing and selling documents they knew belonged to Henley. The defense argued that this was a weak case, with lawyer Antonia Apps calling it the weakest criminal case I have seen in my entire career. Don Henley took the stand for three days, asserting his ownership of the lyrics. He claimed he never gifted or sold them and maintained they were always his property. Henley's lawyers waived attorney-client privilege, releasing about 6,000 pages of internal communications between him and his team to both sides within a few days. The defense pointed out that these emails revealed Henley had initially suspected someone else was responsible for the missing lyrics before being reminded of the book. They also showed that some of Henley's lawyers and a private investigator referred to the disappearance as a burglary, without mentioning Sanders' contract, in an attempt to help their case. Prosecutors have dropped the case against Don Henley over his handwritten Hotel California lyrics, citing delayed disclosures that revealed new information relevant to the defense. This move has been hailed as a display of integrity by the DA's team. Assistant District Attorney Aaron Ginandes explained in court that the delayed disclosures were crucial in allowing the defense to explore key evidence. Witnesses and their lawyers had allegedly used attorney-client privilege to conceal damaging information, which prosecutors believe they were manipulated into hiding. The Manhattan DA's office has been holding onto the lyric sheets since Henley sued for their return. A judge recently threw out a malicious prosecution suit brought by Horowitz against Henley and his manager, Azoff. This ruling effectively left the ownership of the lyric sheets in limbo. As the case continues to unfold, Henley's lawyer has vowed to take the fight into civil court. The DA's office is now deciding what to do with the lyrics, which remain in their custody despite the judge's earlier decision on probable cause. The handwritten lyrics to Don Henley's iconic song Hotel California" remain at the center of a contentious dispute between the songwriter and former music manager Irving Azoff. A judge had previously ruled that the Manhattan District Attorney's office should return the pages to their rightful owner, but they are still in custody. A decision on what to do with the lyrics is now pending, as the DA's office weighs its next move following a court ruling that found probable cause for the prosecution of Henley and Azoff. articles.content: Anthropic's AI agent Claude is set to become a more integral member of team meetings in the near future. The company has announced plans to integrate Claude into meeting calls, allowing it to take notes and update documents in real-time. Claude Meetings will enable teams to add the AI agent to their calls, where it can assist with note-taking and document updates during discussions. The company has confirmed that Claude Meetings will be available on Team and Enterprise plans, but with varying levels of control over who can access the feature. In addition to Whiteboards, Claude can now create shareable spreadsheets from prompts and edit them within cells with trackable changes. Anthropic's focus on enterprise clients has allowed it to maintain a lead over its competitors in this space, and its latest release is tailored to meet the needs of large-scale companies. This allows companies to standardize metrics and avoid conflicting data, making it easier for teams to access a live source of truth. The tool is designed to surface data stories and provide up-to-date numbers that can be accessed by all team members. According to Anthropic, the Data tool will allow colleagues to see the most recent numbers without having to run new queries. This feature, called live sharing, enables viewers to see the results of approved queries while preventing them from running unauthorized ones with elevated access. The company's focus on enterprise clients has led it to prioritize features that cater specifically to this audience. For Team plans, all three features - Data, Whiteboards, and Sheets - are turned on by default. However, for Enterprise plans, only the Data tool will be enabled starting November 19. The settings for Whiteboards and Sheets can still be adjusted in Artifacts. Anthropic's recent releases have been geared towards workplace and productivity software for large-scale companies, which is a departure from OpenAI's focus on consumer products. Anthropic is expanding its collaboration features to make it easier for teams to work together using its AI model Claude. articles.content: As a travel editor, I've spent years exploring far-flung destinations around the world, but California remains a mystery to me, until now. My sole previous visit to the Golden State was a brief trip to Napa Valley, which left an indelible impression of rolling hills and rich wine country. The allure of sunny San Diego beckoned this fall when one of my closest friends announced her wedding plans in the city. The neighborhood's laid-back atmosphere and stunning coastal views were major draws, making it the perfect base for our California adventure. The quiet street off La Jolla's main road was lined with tall trees, providing a serene atmosphere that immediately set us at ease as we arrived at Hamilton I in our Uber. A short walk from downtown San Diego, where we had spent the previous two days, this neighborhood offered a distinct energy that was a welcome change of pace. The shaka sign is often associated with California's laid-back vibe, and walking into Hamilton I felt like we were getting a taste of it. Upon entering our home through the keypad at the front door, we noticed the abundance of natural light pouring in, illuminating the living room's walls adorned with beach-inspired artwork. The spacious backyard is undoubtedly the crowning jewel of this beachy bungalow in La Jolla. Accessible through a sliding door in the living room, it offers an ideal spot to soak up the California sunshine. The compact but well-designed outdoor space boasts a variety of amenities that cater to different needs and preferences. Guests can choose from adjustable lounge chairs, a small dipping pool, or an outdoor dining table next to a barbecue. Alternatively, they can unwind in the lounge area with a firepit, perfect for chilly evenings. Depending on the time of day, each spot offers a unique experience, allowing visitors to make the most of their stay. Despite its proximity to a busy street, the backyard feels like a tranquil oasis thanks to the lush greenery surrounding it. The walls of foliage effectively block out any noise from outside, creating an idyllic setting that's perfect for relaxation or socializing with family and friends. During our three-day stay at Hamilton I, my husband and I made the most of La Jolla's top attractions by walking or taking a short Uber ride to explore the area.
